教學可從單管操作開始：選取一支特定音高的塑料管，以手、地面或身體其他部位敲擊管端: Teaching can start with a single tube: choose one plastic tube of a particular pitch and strike its end with the hand, the floor or another part of the body; the longer the tube the lower the pitch, the shorter the higher. If an octave cap is fitted over one end, the pitch drops an octave. For a start, practise striking a given note steadily, then strike at exactly the moment the teacher indicates, combining with other tubes to make a melody. More advanced players arrange several tubes as a set and strike them with mallets on a purpose-made stand, rather like a xylophone laid out horizontally.

音律管主要由輕質塑膠材料製成，採用中空管狀結構設計。管身採用食品級聚氯乙烯（PV: The boomwhacker is mainly made of lightweight plastic, in a hollow tubular design. The tube is food-grade polyvinyl chloride (PVC) or polypropylene (PP), durable and safe. The surface carries a colour-coded coating so that the different pitches are easy to identify. The end face is smooth and flat, so that it can be struck directly to make a sound. The hollow cavity sounds by the vibration of the air inside, with no metal or wooden internal parts. The whole thing uses recyclable plastic, is light and easy to carry, and suits both teaching and performance.
音律管於美國發展，屬敲擊氣鳴與體鳴樂器。1990年代回收樂器樂團流行，學校以管材: The boomwhacker developed in the United States and counts as a struck aerophone and an idiophone. In the 1990s recycled-instrument groups were popular, and schools made simple instruments from tubing themselves, but it was laborious. Craig Ramsell had the idea in 1994 of using plastic mailing tubes instead; with his wife Monnie he founded DrumSpirit to market them. The original version appeared in 1995, a more durable version in 1997, Whacky Music was founded in 1998, and in 1999 octave caps extended the range. In 2009 the trademark passed to Rhythm Band Instruments.
音律管是美國出現的輕量空心塑膠管敲擊樂器，依長度調音並以顏色區分，H-S 編號: The boomwhacker is a lightweight hollow plastic tube percussion instrument that appeared in the United States, tuned by length and coded by colour, H-S number 413, counting among the aerophones as a plosive aerophone and also in the idiophone family. The player strikes the end of a tube with the hand, the floor or the body, and may also strike several tubes laid out on a stand with mallets. It is common in primary-school music classrooms, where pupils each hold a tube of a different pitch; it is also used by performing groups and in training for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
音律管音色明亮清脆，具有獨特的塑膠質感與輕盈的音質特徵。其音域跨度廣闊，從低沉的: The boomwhacker has a bright, clear timbre with a distinctive plastic quality and a light, airy sound. Its range is wide, from a deep tenor to a bright high, the pitch changing step by step with the length of the tube. Struck, it produces a warm resonance, the sound coming from the vibration of the air inside the hollow tube. Compared with the dryness of a xylophone, the boomwhacker is softer and warmer; compared with the dullness of percussion, it is more transparent and bright. What is distinctive is a rhythmic, undulating quality in the timbre: it has the direct attack of percussion and still keeps the resonance of a wind instrument. The overall sound is light and lively, fits easily into any style, and is especially good at creating a cheerful, childlike atmosphere.
